bib.title: Rephrase and Respond: Let Large Language Models Ask Better Questions for Themselves

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Rephrase and Respond: Let Large Language Models Ask Better Questions for Themselves", Yihe Deng, Weitong Zhang, Zixiang Chen, Quanquan Gu (UCLA). arXiv:2311.04205v2 (18 Apr 2024), labelled "Preprint". Original 2023.

COVERAGE: All 25 pages, 84,396 chars, read in full (body, Appendix A, B, C tables of I/O examples). Reference list skimmed only. The tool-result dump was cut at 40k chars, so I re-extracted the rest. The last pages (Tables 17-22) are per-task I/O examples. I read them but they hold no new numbers. Caveat: the extraction rendered Figure 4/5/7 as unlabeled number clouds. Only Table 1 and the in-text numbers are reliable for per-task values. Figures 5/7 values are not usable.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- RaR (one prompt: rephrase and answer) lifts GPT-4 average zero-shot accuracy over 10 tasks from 64.95 to 89.77.
  number: 64.95 -> 89.77 avg (+24.8 points)
  setup: GPT-4 (API accessed 10/01-10/30 2023), zero-shot, 10 tasks, most with 105-220 sampled questions. Tasks: Even day/month/year, Compare age, CSQA, Dates, Sports, Last letter (2), Last letter (4), Coin flip.
  quote: "Original 54.29 58.10 57.14 98.44 84.09 69.92 79.55 52.05 21.36 74.55 64.95 / RaR 93.33 83.96 89.52 100 85.45 75.88 84.54 99.09 86.82 99.09 89.77"
  where: Table 1, p6
- Biggest gains are on tasks with ambiguous or poorly posed questions. Well-posed ones barely move. Last letter (4) goes 21.36 -> 86.82, Last letter (2) 52.05 -> 99.09, Coin flip 74.55 -> 99.09, Even day 54.29 -> 93.33. CSQA goes only 84.09 -> 85.45, and Compare age 98.44 -> 100.
  number: see left
  quote: "A larger margin indicates a less well-designed question. For tasks such as CSQA where the question quality is good enough, our method still offers a marginal improvement."
  where: Fig 4 caption, p6; Table 1
- The gain does not depend on the exact wording. Four paraphrased RaR prompts all beat baseline, averaging 87.17 to 88.97 versus 89.77 for the main prompt. Deviations are -0.8 to -2.6.
  quote: "RaR1 94.29 82.08 ... 87.85(−1.92) ... RaR3 85.71 ... 87.17(−2.6)"
  where: Table 1, p6. Note that RaR3 is worse than the main prompt by 2.6 and, on Even day, lower than the other variants (85.71).
- Gains scale with model strength. With Two-step RaR, GPT-4-0613 gains most, GPT-3.5-turbo-0613 less, Vicuna-13b-v1.5 modestly. GPT-3.5 and Vicuna get slightly worse on some tasks, such as Sports.
  quote: "On certain tasks such as Sports, GPT-3.5 and Vicuna even exhibit slightly diminished performance." and "all models can benefit from rephrasing questions, with more advanced models expected to gain a larger improvement."
  where: Sec 4.3, p6-7. Vicuna's Last letter (4) is excluded because of near-zero accuracy. Per-task numbers are not recoverable from the extraction.
- Two-step RaR transfers: questions rephrased by GPT-4 help the weaker Vicuna-13b-v1.5 more than its own rephrasings do.
  number: Even day 58.10 -> 61.90; Even month 56.19 -> 60.95; CSQA 51.36 -> 55.00; Sports 65.00 -> 73.64; Dates 32.79 -> 37.67; Last letter (2) 5.45 -> 10.45
  quote: "Vicuna-rephrased 58.10 56.19 51.36 65.00 32.79 5.45 / GPT-4-rephrased 61.90 60.95 55.00 73.64 37.67 10.45"
  where: Table 2, p8. Even year was dropped because Vicuna's rephrasings were already as clear as GPT-4's. Absolute accuracies stay low.
- Zero-shot CoT ("Let's think step by step") can fail where RaR helps. GPT-4 on Chinese Idiom (infer the masked first character) scores 32.38 original, 31.43 zero-shot CoT, 35.24 RaR. The authors attribute the CoT drop to hallucination in the intermediate steps.
  quote: "Chinese Idiom Accuracy (%) 32.38 31.43 35.24"
  where: Table 3, p8. These gaps are small on a 105-item set, and the paper gives no significance test.
- StereoSet (220 inter-sentence samples), GPT-4: Language Modeling Score 84.09 original, 84.09 CoT, 97.73 RaR. Fair Score (picking neither stereotype option) 6.82 original, 35.00 CoT, 42.27 RaR.
  quote: "StereoSet Language Modeling Score (%) 84.09 84.09 97.73Fair Score (%) 6.82 35.00 42.27"
  where: Table 3, p8. "Fair Score" is the authors' own metric, added because GPT-4 sometimes said neither option could be concluded.
- RaR combined with few-shot CoT rescues flawed exemplars. Exemplars were Wei et al. 2022's last-letter examples with the reasoning altered to "first letter" while keeping the answers. GPT-4 follows the bad logic. Adding RaR (the rephrase step also repairs the examples) restores accuracy.
  number: one-shot 89.04 / 78.18 (last letter 2 / 4) -> RaR+one-shot 100 / 93.64; four-shot 87.21 / 52.27 -> RaR+four-shot 100 / 95.45
  quote: "Four-shot CoT 87.21 52.27 / RaR+Four-shot CoT 100 95.45"
  where: Table 4, p9. Tables 7-8 give the exemplars. The flaws were deliberately injected.
- RaR is complementary to zero-shot CoT: combine by adding "let's think step by step" to the RaR prompt. This is asserted. No separate combined table for zero-shot CoT appears in the text I read.
  where: Sec 6.1, p8
- Weak models rephrase badly. GPT-3.5 misread "even month" as even number of days and added a wrong "recent game" constraint. In 45/220 Sports and 21/369 Dates questions it appended "Please rephrase...", so the answer was just another rephrase. The authors deleted all sentences containing "rephrase" for GPT-3.5 on those two datasets. Vicuna changed "yesterday" to "today".
  quote: "GPT-3.5 tends to introduce the following phrase to rephrased questions in Sports (45 out of 220) and Dates (21 out of 369)"
  where: App B.1, p15-16
- Iterating the rephrase: repeated Two-step rephrasing by GPT-4 converges toward a consistent clarification of "even day" by the third round, and questions get more elaborate. Demonstrated on one example question (Table 10). No accuracy numbers.
  where: App B.2, p16-17
- Motivating example: GPT-4 misreads "even month" in several ways (Feb is "odd" for irregular days; even/odd means days in the month). Fig 2 says self-rephrased questions answer the 105-celebrity task far better. No numbers are quoted in the text for Fig 2.
  where: Fig 1-2, p2

PROMPT TEMPLATES (verbatim)
- 1-step RaR (eq 3.1): "{question}"\nRephrase and expand the question, and respond.
- Variants: "Reword and elaborate on the inquiry, then provide an answer." / "Reframe the question with additional context and detail, then provide an answer." / "Modify the original question for clarity and detail, then offer an answer." / "Restate and elaborate on the inquiry before proceeding with a response."
- Two-step, step 1 (rephraser): "{question}"\nGiven the above question, rephrase and expand it to help you do better answering. Maintain all information in the original question.
- Two-step, step 2 (responder): (original) {question}\n(rephrased) {rephrased question}\nUse your answer for the rephrased question to answer the original question.
- RaR+CoT: add "let's think step by step" to 3.1.
- Format suffixes appended to both baseline and RaR (Table 6): Dates "Final answer format should be MM/DD/YYYY."; CSQA and StereoSet "Select the *single* most sensible answer."; Sports and Coin flip "Answer the Yes or No question."
- Task data details: Even day/month/year 105 questions each, Compare age 104, CSQA 220, Dates 369 (full set, no choices given), Last letter (2)/(4), Coin flip and Sports 220 each. Coin flip has "Flip means reverse." appended.

LIMITS
- Models are GPT-4 (Oct 2023), GPT-4-0613, GPT-3.5-turbo-0613 and Vicuna-13b-v1.5, all long dated. Nothing on reasoning models or modern models.
- Small samples (105-220 per task, random subsets). No confidence intervals, seeds or significance tests. Single runs are implied.
- The Even day/month/year and Compare age data were generated by GPT-4 itself, not from an open benchmark (footnote 1: "As the data are not open-sourced, we let GPT-4 generate 105 famous individuals with their birth dates and 105 Chinese idioms in its knowledge."). The ground truth was not independently verified in the text.
- Scoring is exact-match plus manual checking. The sports/coin-flip tasks add a format suffix.
- Dates is the harder no-choices version, so it is not comparable to published numbers.
- The authors concede weaker models gain little or lose on some tasks. Vicuna's self-rephrasing is poor. They say more exploration is needed on its capability.
- Cost, latency and extra tokens are not measured. 1-step RaR makes outputs longer. Two-step adds a call.
- Comparison to CoT is narrow: zero-shot CoT is tested on only two extra tasks (Chinese Idiom, StereoSet), and the main 10-task table has no CoT column. The conclusion mentions "mathematical formulation" comparisons with CoT, but I found none in the extracted text.
- Not tested against self-consistency or other prompt-optimisation methods. Compared only in prose with APE-style iterative methods.
- Table 13's headline example shows Two-step RaR still failing on some items (Obama, Kahlo). Table 12 shows 1-step RaR failing on da Vinci while giving a self-contradicting answer ("Yes... odd-numbered day").

BUILDS ON (as printed)
Allen-Zhu & Li 2023 (Physics of language models 3.2; tasks and motivating example); Kojima et al. 2022 (zero-shot CoT); Wei et al. 2022 (few-shot CoT, last-letter exemplars); Zhou et al. 2022b (APE) and Pryzant et al. 2023 (iterative prompt refinement, contrasted); Sorensen et al. 2022; Madaan et al. 2023 (Self-Refine) and Shinn et al. 2023 (contrasted: post-hoc self-correction); Huang et al. 2023 and Stechly et al. 2023 (self-correction limits); Weston & Sukhbaatar 2023 (System 2 Attention, concurrent); Yu et al. 2023a and Prasad et al. 2023 (concurrent rephrasing); Pawelczyk et al. 2023 (bad few-shot examples); Turpin et al. 2023 (CoT reliability); Nadeem et al. 2021 (StereoSet); Shaikh et al. 2022 (prompt format for StereoSet); Druckman 2001 (framing, for "frames in thought"); Talmor et al. 2019 (CSQA); bench authors 2023 (Dates, Sports); Fortes 2023 (last letter data); Zhou et al. 2023 (Foresee and Reflect).

CODE: none, beyond the prompt templates above.

FIGURES (p numbers as printed)
- Fig 1 (p2): GPT-4 gives contradictory justifications for "even month". Shows ambiguity as the failure cause.
- Fig 2 (p2): original vs self-rephrased question for even day, month and year. It shows what a rephrase looks like, e.g. listing "2nd, 4th, 6th, 8th".
- Fig 3 (p5): RaR demo on "Edgar Bob" last letters. Shows the single-prompt shape.
- Fig 4 (p6): bar chart of GPT-4 original vs RaR over 10 tasks. Same data as Table 1.
- Fig 5 / Fig 7 (p7, p15): GPT-4-0613, GPT-3.5, Vicuna with Two-step RaR. Numbers are garbled in the extraction.
- Fig 6 (p9): a bad few-shot exemplar (first-letter logic) misleads GPT-4, and RaR repairs it. Best single picture of the exemplar-repair claim.

PROBLEMS: Figures 4, 5 and 7 come out as unordered numbers, so per-model per-task values (Fig 5/7) are not reliably readable and I omitted them. Two-step prompt references in App B.2 appear as "(??)" (broken cross-reference). The paper's text contains no embedded instructions.
